## Orchestration: the pipeline

On the active MGMT, in PowerShell 7, from `C:\MidCoastLab\repo`. Every entry point validates the inventory and the live site first, writes a transcript to `C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Logs\Orchestration`, and asks for the vault's master password when the vault is locked.

### `orchestration/Build-LabTemplate.ps1`

Builds a new version of a golden template (WIN2022-TEMPLATE or WIN11-TEMPLATE) with Packer.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Templates are versioned, because VMs are linked clones of the version they
were built from and Proxmox can't delete a template that has linked clones.
1. Validates inventory and the site; deletes superseded versions that no VM
   uses any more.
2. Removes any leftover staging VM, then runs Packer at the template's
   staging VMID (templates.<key>.build.staging_vmid_offset in lab.yaml).
3. On success: full-clones staging into the next free VMID of the template's
   range as <family>-<YYMMDD>-<NN>, converts it to a template, records it in
   the ledger as current (the previous version becomes superseded), and
   deletes staging.
New VMs clone the current version; existing VMs keep theirs until they are
replaced. A failed build changes nothing.

Run monthly, or after critical security updates. Build one template at a
time: every template family shares the Packer build slot on MGMT.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Template <string>` |  | `'windows_server_2022'` | The template to build: a key under templates: in lab.yaml (windows_server_2022, windows_11, or any template added later). Default: windows_server_2022. |

```powershell
./orchestration/Build-LabTemplate.ps1 -Template windows_server_2022   # WIN2022-TEMPLATE
./orchestration/Build-LabTemplate.ps1 -Template windows_11            # WIN11-TEMPLATE
```

### `orchestration/Invoke-LabDcRotation.ps1`

Replaces a domain controller with a fresh one from the current WIN2022 template, in two stages with a checkpoint between them.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Run on the active MGMT, in an elevated PowerShell 7 window (the last step of
Add points this machine's own DNS client at the new set of DCs).

Add      builds the replacement and moves everything onto it:
  1. Pre-flight: inventory, site, both DCs pass validation, a free DC slot,
     the current WIN2022 template exists.
  2. Picks the DC to replace (the oldest, or -Replace <name>) and allocates
     DC-<today>-NN in the free slot (ledger: building, replaces <old>).
  3. Terraform clones it; it bootstraps as a replica of the DC that stays,
     and is gated on its own validation (ledger: active).
  4. Moves every FSMO role the old DC holds to the new one (and with the PDC
     emulator, the external time source).
  5. Marks the old DC retiring and points every DNS client in the lab (DCs,
     every other lab machine, this MGMT) at the new set of DCs.
  6. Re-validates the active DCs.
  The old DC keeps running as a third DC until Retire. Check anything you
  like in between; nothing depends on it any more.

Retire   removes the old DC: moves any FSMO role still on it, demotes it,
         removes its leftover DNS records and computer object, destroys the
         VM and drops it from the ledger.

Abort    (before Retire) undoes Add: the old DC becomes active again, FSMO
         and DNS clients move back, and the replacement is demoted and
         destroyed, the same way Retire removes a DC.

Every stage can be re-run after a failure; it picks up where it stopped.
-Force (Retire/Abort only) handles a DC that can't be reached: FSMO roles
are seized and its metadata is cleaned out of AD instead of a demotion.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Stage <Add | Retire | Abort>` | yes |  | Add, Retire or Abort; see above. |
| `-Replace <string>` |  |  | Add: the active DC to replace (default: the oldest). |
| `-Retry` |  |  | Add: resume a replacement whose bootstrap failed. |
| `-Force` |  |  | Retire/Abort: the DC being removed can't be reached; seize and clean up. |

```powershell
./orchestration/Invoke-LabDcRotation.ps1 -Stage Add
./orchestration/Invoke-LabDcRotation.ps1 -Stage Retire
./orchestration/Invoke-LabDcRotation.ps1 -Stage Add -Replace DC-261028-01
```

### `orchestration/Invoke-LabMgmtRotation.ps1`

Replaces MGMT, the machine that runs the pipeline, with a fresh one built from WIN11-TEMPLATE.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

MGMT can't destroy and rebuild itself, so the replacement runs in three stages:

Prepare   run on the CURRENT MGMT
  1. Validates inventory; records the hand-built MGMT-00 in the ledger if needed.
  2. Checks WIN11-TEMPLATE exists and at least one DC is active.
  3. Allocates the replacement in the spare MGMT slot (e.g. MGMT-YYMMDD-00, .31).
  4. terraform apply: clones it.
  5. Bootstraps it (toolchain, Remote Desktop, domain join, LAPS) and gates on validation.
  6. Hands over: ledger (new = active, old = retiring), the repo with git history,
     Terraform state and the KeePass vault, each copied and hash-verified.
  7. Locks this MGMT: from now on it refuses every pipeline action except Abort.

Complete  run on the NEW MGMT (sign in as your -a account over Remote Desktop)
  1. Checks it is the active MGMT and can reach Proxmox and every DC.
  2. terraform init, and confirms the handed-over state matches the ledger
     (any create or delete stops it; in-place updates are only warned about).
  3. Retires the old MGMT: shuts it down, destroys the VM (Terraform, or the
     Proxmox API if it was hand-built) and confirms it's gone, then removes its
     computer object and DNS records. With -KeepOld it is only shut down; run Complete again later
     to destroy it.

Abort     run on the OLD MGMT, any time before Complete destroys it
  Unlocks it, marks it active again, destroys the replacement and removes its
  computer object. Anything done ON the new MGMT after the handover (Terraform
  changes, ledger edits) is lost, so Abort after handover needs -Force.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Stage <Prepare | Complete | Abort>` | yes |  | Prepare (on the current MGMT), Complete (on the new MGMT) or Abort (on the old MGMT); see above. |
| `-Retry` |  |  | Prepare: resume a replacement whose bootstrap failed, from the failed stage. |
| `-KeepOld` |  |  | Complete: shut the old MGMT down but keep its VM for now. |
| `-Force` |  |  | Abort: roll back even though the handover already happened. |

```powershell
./orchestration/Invoke-LabMgmtRotation.ps1 -Stage Prepare     # on the current MGMT
./orchestration/Invoke-LabMgmtRotation.ps1 -Stage Complete    # on the new MGMT
./orchestration/Invoke-LabMgmtRotation.ps1 -Stage Abort -Force
```

### `orchestration/Invoke-LabPhase.ps1`

Runs a deployment phase: inventory validation -> Terraform -> bootstrap -> validation.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Phase 1 (ActiveDirectory) builds the forest from nothing:
  1. Validate inventory; allocate two DC instances in the ledger (slots A, B).
  2. terraform apply: clone both VMs from WIN2022-TEMPLATE.
  3. First DC: push platform + metadata (dc_mode=forest) + secrets; wait;
     gate on its validation report (Critical = stop).
  4. Second DC: same, dc_mode=replica, replicating from the first.
  Each DC is marked active in the ledger as soon as its own bootstrap and
  validation pass.
  5. Point every DC's DNS client at its partner(s) first, loopback last;
     re-validate all DCs. Critical failures stop the run.

Re-running is safe: instances already active are skipped; -Retry resumes
a DC whose bootstrap failed, from the stage that failed. If every DC is
already active (e.g. only the final validation failed), -Retry re-runs
step 5 alone.

Phases 2 and 3 are not implemented yet.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Phase <1 | 2 | 3>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Retry` |  |  |  |
| `-PlanOnly` |  |  | Show the Terraform plan and stop. |

```powershell
./orchestration/Invoke-LabPhase.ps1 -Phase 1
./orchestration/Invoke-LabPhase.ps1 -Phase 1 -Retry
```

### `orchestration/Reset-LabLedger.ps1`

Resets the ledger and Terraform state after a lab has been torn down, so the pipeline can build again from nothing (runbook, "Starting over").

Runs: PowerShell 7.

proxmox-teardown.sh destroys the lab's VMs on Proxmox, but the ledger
(inventory/instances.yaml) lives in the repo and still lists the old DCs,
MGMT and template versions, and C:\MidCoastLab\state still holds Terraform
state for them. The next Invoke-LabPhase then believes the lab is deployed
(issue #20). This script:
  1. Asks Proxmox about every VMID the ledger lists. It REFUSES to run if any
     listed instance or template still exists, so it can't wipe a live lab:
     retire machines with the rotations, or tear the site down first.
  2. Empties instances:, drops every template version that is gone from
     Proxmox (a version that still exists is kept), removes the Terraform
     state file and its backup, and the handover and CERT lock files.
  3. Commits the ledger (git add + commit; push is left to you).
Run it on the machine that will run the pipeline next (MGMT-00 of the new
build), after Initialize-LabRepo.ps1. A fresh clone of your repo carries
the old ledger too, so a new MGMT-00 needs it as much as an old one.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-PlanOnly` |  |  | Show what would change; write nothing. |
| `-SkipProxmox` |  |  | Don't ask Proxmox whether the listed VMs exist (for a ledger that belongs to a Proxmox you can no longer reach). Dangerous with a live lab: without the check, nothing stops the reset. Prefer tearing down, then resetting. |

```powershell
./orchestration/Reset-LabLedger.ps1 -PlanOnly
./orchestration/Reset-LabLedger.ps1
```

### `orchestration/Test-LabInventory.ps1`

Inventory validation: syntax, schema and semantic rules, for the product design (lab.yaml), the site settings (site.yaml), and the resolved result.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Runs before every pipeline action. Errors stop the pipeline; warnings
don't. Returns the findings; exits 1 when run directly with errors.

Site checks: required values, no placeholders, subnet size, gateway,
VMID base, ISO names, and that site.yaml holds only site settings. Product
checks: lab.yaml holds no site settings. Then every semantic rule runs on
the resolved inventory.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-InventoryPath <string>` |  |  |  |
| `-SitePath <string>` |  |  |  |
| `-LedgerPath <string>` |  |  |  |
| `-PassThru` |  |  |  |

```powershell
./orchestration/Test-LabInventory.ps1 -SitePath ./inventory/site.template.yaml
```

### `orchestration/Test-LabSite.ps1`

Live pre-flight check of the site: does this Proxmox and this network match site.yaml, and is everything the lab will claim actually free?

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Runs from MGMT with the provisioning token. Checks:
  Proxmox  API and token, node, storages (content types), bridge, ISO files,
           pool; every lab VMID is either free or already the lab's own
           (in the pool, tagged midcoast-lab)
  Network  no device outside the lab answers on a lab address (ping + ARP),
           the gateway answers, the DNS forwarders resolve

The token only sees VMs in the lab's pool, so for VMIDs it can't see it
asks Proxmox whether the ID is free. If Proxmox won't say (permissions),
that VMID is reported as unverified: the root-side check in the site kit's
proxmox-setup.sh is authoritative.

Invoke-LabPhase, Build-LabTemplate and Invoke-LabMgmtRotation run this
automatically; errors stop them.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-SkipNetwork` |  |  |  |
| `-PassThru` |  |  |  |

```powershell
./orchestration/Test-LabSite.ps1 -SkipNetwork      # Proxmox checks only
```

## Setup: workstation and MGMT-00

`New-LabSiteKit.ps1` on your workstation (PowerShell 7 + powershell-yaml); the `setup/mgmt` scripts on MGMT-00, once each, in the order the runbook gives.

### `setup/New-LabSiteKit.ps1`

Generates the site kit: a filled-in runbook and the Proxmox setup script, from inventory/lab.yaml + inventory/site.yaml.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Run on any machine with PowerShell 7 and the powershell-yaml module (your
workstation is fine; MGMT-00 doesn't exist yet). It validates the
inventory, resolves it, and writes:

  out/site-kit/<site>/RUNBOOK.md        docs/runbook.md with every value filled in
  out/site-kit/<site>/proxmox-setup.sh  the Proxmox setup script with this site's values

Re-run it after any change to site.yaml. out/ is gitignored.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-SitePath <string>` |  |  |  |
| `-OutputRoot <string>` |  |  |  |

```powershell
Install-Module powershell-yaml -Scope CurrentUser    # once
./setup/New-LabSiteKit.ps1
```

### `setup/mgmt/Initialize-LabRepo.ps1`

Puts the repo where the pipeline expects it on MGMT-00, as a git repository, with a git identity (runbook step 5).

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Run from any copy of the repo (a clone, an extracted zip, a copied folder)
on MGMT-00, in a normal PowerShell 7 window, after Install-MgmtTools.ps1.
1. Copies this folder to the repo path from lab.yaml (handover.repo_path,
   C:\MidCoastLab\repo) unless it is already there, including site.yaml.
2. Makes it a git repository if it isn't one (a copied or extracted folder
   has no .git), sets core.filemode=false (a clone copied from Linux would
   otherwise show every .sh file as modified), and commits everything. You don't need a remote: the
   pipeline only needs the local history. Add a private remote later if you
   want a copy elsewhere (README, Requirements).
3. Sets git's user.name and user.email for your account, from site.yaml's
   administrator (given name, surname, <username>@<tenant domain>), unless
   you set them already.
4. Runs Test-LabInventory.ps1 from the new location.

```powershell
cd C:\Users\LabAdmin\Downloads\midcoast-labs
./setup/mgmt/Initialize-LabRepo.ps1
```

### `setup/mgmt/Initialize-LabVault.ps1`

Creates the KeePass vault if needed, registers it for your account, and fills in every secret the inventory names (runbook step 6; again for each new account or MGMT).

Runs: PowerShell 7.

1. If the database doesn't exist yet, creates it with keepassxc-cli (asks
   for a new master password, twice; at least 12 characters). Keep that
   password outside the lab: without it and the .kdbx, the lab's secrets
   are gone.
2. Registers the database as the SecretManagement vault named in lab.yaml
   (secrets.vault) for the account running this script, and unlocks it.
   A wrong master password is asked again (three tries), and nothing is
   written until the vault really opens.
3. For each secret the inventory names:
     - Proxmox token secrets: asks you (paste from proxmox-setup.sh's output)
     - the Tailscale auth key, when site.yaml tailscale.enabled: asks you
     - your administrators' <username> and <username>-a accounts: asks
       whether to generate each password or let you choose it (12+
       characters, three character classes); -GeneratePasswords skips the
       question and generates them all
     - everything else (built-in Administrator, DSRM, service accounts):
       generates a random 24-character password
   Existing entries are never changed.
4. Sets your git identity from site.yaml (Set-LabGitIdentity), since this
   runs once per account on every MGMT.

Run it again on a new MGMT, or as a new account: it then only registers the
existing vault and reports every entry as 'exists'.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-DatabasePath <string>` | yes |  | The .kdbx file, outside the repo: lab.yaml handover.vault_path (C:\MidCoastLab\MidCoastLab.kdbx). |
| `-GeneratePasswords` |  |  | Generate every account password without asking, including your own <username> and <username>-a accounts (read them later with Get-Secret -Vault <vault> -Name <account> -AsPlainText). |

```powershell
./setup/mgmt/Initialize-LabVault.ps1 -DatabasePath C:\MidCoastLab\MidCoastLab.kdbx
```

### `setup/mgmt/Install-MgmtTools.ps1`

Installs the MGMT toolchain on the hand-built MGMT-00 (runbook step 5).

Runs: elevated.

A thin wrapper. The implementation is platform/roles/mgmt-tools.ps1,
the same script a pipeline-built MGMT runs during bootstrap, so the
hand-built MGMT-00 and every replacement get an identical toolchain:
PowerShell 7, Git, Terraform, Packer, VS Code, KeePassXC, the ADK
Deployment Tools (oscdimg.exe), RSAT and the PowerShell modules.

Run once, in an elevated Windows PowerShell, from any copy of the repo. It
also creates C:\MidCoastLab and grants your account access, so the steps
that follow don't need elevation. Then open a NEW PowerShell 7 window (the
PATH changed) and continue with setup/mgmt/Initialize-LabRepo.ps1.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Versions <object>` |  |  | Versions default to "latest". To match pinned versions in lab.yaml (MGMT software_versions), pass them, e.g. .\Install-MgmtTools.ps1 -Versions @{ terraform = '1.9.8'; packer = '1.11.2' } |
| `-Rsat <string[]>` |  | `@('standard')` | 'standard' (default: AD DS/LDS, DNS, Group Policy, Server Manager), 'all' (every RSAT tool; 3+ hours), or capability names, e.g. .\Install-MgmtTools.ps1 -Rsat standard, 'Rsat.Dhcp.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0' Keep it the same as lab.yaml's MGMT rsat, so every MGMT gets the same tools. |

### `setup/mgmt/Join-LabDomain.ps1`

Joins the hand-built MGMT-00 to the lab domain and applies everything a pipeline-built MGMT gets after its join (runbook step 8).

Runs: elevated, PowerShell 7.

Run once on MGMT-00, in an ELEVATED PowerShell 7 window, after Phase 1.
1. Points this machine's DNS client at the active DCs (from the ledger) and
   waits until the domain answers.
2. Joins the domain into the MGMT placement OU (Admin/Tier0/Devices) with
   svc-domainjoin, whose password comes from the vault.
3. Registers a one-shot task that runs as SYSTEM at the next start-up and
   applies the post-join rules, the same ones every pipeline-built MGMT gets
   (platform/roles/mgmt.ps1 and the handover): the Tier 0 admin group may use
   Remote Desktop, git may use the repo under any account (safe.directory),
   and only SYSTEM, Administrators and the Tier 0 admin group may use
   C:\MidCoastLab. They need the domain, so they run after the restart and
   log to C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Logs\Bootstrap\mgmt00-postjoin.log.
4. Restarts the machine. Sign in as <you>-a afterwards (runbook step 8).

Before you run it, have a way back in: the local account's password
(printed by proxmox-setup.sh) and your -a account's password from the vault.
The script shows that reminder and asks you to confirm.

Re-runnable: already joined -> only the post-join task is (re)registered.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-NoRestart` |  |  | Don't restart at the end (the post-join rules then wait for your restart). |

### `setup/mgmt/Join-LabTailnet.ps1`

Puts the hand-built MGMT-00 on the site's tailnet the way every lab machine is (site.yaml tailscale.enabled), with the reusable key from the vault (runbook step 6).

Runs: elevated, PowerShell 7.

Pipeline-built machines join during their bootstrap; MGMT-00 is built before
the vault exists, so it gets this step here, once, after Initialize-LabVault.
Same settings as every other lab machine (Lab.System Install-LabTailscale):
--unattended --accept-routes=false --accept-dns=false, the Tailscale adapter
kept out of DNS, Remote Desktop allowed on that adapter only, the AuthKey
system policy and the MidCoastLab-Tailscale watchdog task, so a restart or
an update can't log it out.

If proxmox-setup.sh already joined MGMT-00 with a one-time key (runbook
step 3), this re-authenticates it with the vault's reusable key and adds the
policy and watchdog; the device keeps its name on the tailnet.

The key in the vault must be reusable, tagged and NOT ephemeral: an ephemeral
device drops off the tailnet when it's offline and can't rejoin.

```powershell
./setup/mgmt/Join-LabTailnet.ps1      # elevated PowerShell 7
```

## Setup: the Proxmox node

On the lab's Proxmox node, as root. Run the site kit's copy of `proxmox-setup.sh` (it carries your values); `proxmox-teardown.sh` runs as it is.

### `setup/proxmox/proxmox-setup.sh`

proxmox-setup.sh: one-time Proxmox setup for a MidCoast Lab site.

DON'T run this repo copy. ./setup/New-LabSiteKit.ps1 writes a filled-in copy
to out/site-kit/<site>/proxmox-setup.sh with this site's values at the top.
Copy that one to the lab's Proxmox node and run it there as root:

Pre-flight (as root it sees every VM on the cluster, so it is the
authoritative collision check):
  - running on the lab's node
  - storages exist and accept disk images / ISO images
  - the lab bridge exists
  - every lab VMID is free, or already this lab's (carrying the lab's tag), and the
    pool and user aren't another site's
  - the ISOs are uploaded (Windows 11 + VirtIO are required for MGMT-00)
Setup:
  - pool, least-privilege role, terraform-prov@pve user, API tokens
    (secrets printed ONCE: put them in KeePass), ACLs
  - the MGMT-00 VM, unless it exists or CREATE_MGMT00=0, with an answer CD that
    installs Windows 11 unattended: disk, VirtIO drivers, a local admin account,
    no first-run screens, then guest tools, static address, time zone, name and
    Remote Desktop. The script starts it, waits for the install to finish (about
    20-40 minutes), ejects the install media and deletes the answer CD.
  - with site.yaml tailscale.enabled, MGMT-00 can join your tailnet during that
    install, so you can reach it before anything else exists: the script asks
    for a ONE-TIME (single-use, tagged, not ephemeral) auth key, or takes it from
    the TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY environment variable; leave it empty to skip. The key
    is never written to the site kit; it rides on the answer CD (root-only, shredded
    after the install) and is used once. Runbook step 6 later switches MGMT-00 to the
    vault's reusable key, like every other lab machine.
  - every secret it creates (API tokens, MGMT-00's local password) is printed and
    kept in a root-only file until you've copied it (shred it afterwards)

Safe to re-run: existing objects are updated, tokens are never re-created.

```bash
bash proxmox-setup.sh check   # pre-flight only, changes nothing
bash proxmox-setup.sh         # pre-flight, then set up
bash proxmox-setup.sh finish-mgmt00   # resume waiting for the MGMT-00 install
```

### `setup/proxmox/proxmox-teardown.sh`

proxmox-teardown.sh: removes a MidCoast Lab site from Proxmox, so it can be built
again from scratch. Keeps your ISOs.

Run as root on the lab's node (proxmox.node in site.yaml):

A site with its own names (site.yaml proxmox.pool/role/tag/service_account.user,
1.6) passes them: --pool --user --role --tag. The defaults are the pre-1.6 names.
Your RUNBOOK.md ("Starting over") has the full command for your site.

Removes:
  - every VM in the lab's 150-VMID block (vmid_base .. vmid_base+149) that is the
    lab's (carrying the lab's tag, or in the lab's pool): clones first, then templates;
    stopped first, protection cleared, snapshots and disks with them
  - disks left behind in that block (vm-<id>-*, base-<id>-*) on the VM storages
  - the pool, the provisioning user (and its API tokens), the role
  - MGMT-00's answer CD (midcoast-mgmt00-answer.iso) and any root-only secrets file
    proxmox-setup.sh left behind (/root/midcoast-*-secrets.txt)
  - with --include-backups: vzdump backups of those VMIDs
Never touches: a VM in the block that isn't the lab's (it's listed and skipped), any
other VMID, any other ISO, the storages, bridges or network.

Outside Proxmox (not done here): remove the lab's machines in the Tailscale admin
console, and anything you pointed at lab addresses by hand (router DNS, DHCP leases).

```bash
bash proxmox-teardown.sh --vmid-base 3000            # shows the plan, asks, then removes
bash proxmox-teardown.sh --vmid-base 3000 --dry-run  # shows the plan only
```

## Tools: maintaining the repo

On the machine where you prepare releases (PowerShell 7 and git).

### `tools/Export-LabRelease.ps1`

Exports a release of the product (no site, no ledger) into a folder, for the public repo.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

Takes the files of a commit (default HEAD) from git, not the working tree, so only
committed work is exported. Leaves out everything that describes one lab:
  inventory/site.yaml, inventory/instances.yaml, terraform/.terraform.lock.hcl,
  tools/release-deny.txt
and writes an empty ledger in its place. Everything in -Destination except .git is
replaced, so files removed from the product disappear there too.

Then it scans the result, and refuses (deleting nothing, but listing the hits) if any
file contains:
  - a pattern from tools/release-deny.txt (this site's names, addresses, accounts), or
  - something shaped like a secret: a Tailscale or GitHub key, a private key, a
    Proxmox token with its secret.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Destination <string>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Ref <string>` |  | `'HEAD'` |  |

```powershell
./tools/Export-LabRelease.ps1 -Destination ../midcoast-labs
```

### `tools/New-LabScriptReference.ps1`

Generates docs/scripts.md: every script in the repo, its parameters and switches, where it runs and when, from the scripts' own help.

Runs: PowerShell 7.

The scripts are the source. For each .ps1 it reads the comment-based help
(.SYNOPSIS, .DESCRIPTION, .PARAMETER, .EXAMPLE), the #Requires lines and the
param() block (name, type, default, ValidateSet, mandatory, and the comment
above a parameter when it has no .PARAMETER entry); for each .sh the header
comment and its "bash ..." usage lines. Where a script runs comes from its
folder (orchestration -> the active MGMT, setup/mgmt -> MGMT-00, and so on).

Run it after changing any script's parameters or help, and commit the result
with the change. It refuses a .ps1 without a .SYNOPSIS, so every script stays
documented. Export-LabRelease.ps1 runs it with -Check and refuses to export
while docs/scripts.md is out of date.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Check` |  |  | Don't write; exit 1 if docs/scripts.md differs from what would be written. |

```powershell
./tools/New-LabScriptReference.ps1           # writes docs/scripts.md
./tools/New-LabScriptReference.ps1 -Check    # CI / pre-release check
```

## Platform: inside every guest

Pushed into each guest by the orchestrator and run by the `MidCoastLab-Bootstrap` task as SYSTEM. Not run by hand, except `validate.ps1` (on a guest, elevated) and `tailscale/Enable-LabTailscaleWatchdog.ps1`.

### `platform/bootstrap.ps1`

MidCoast Lab bootstrap. Runs inside every pipeline-built guest.

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

Cloudbase-Init -> bootstrap.ps1 -> role script -> validation script.

The orchestrator pushes the platform (this folder), metadata.json and the
role's secrets over WinRM/HTTPS, registers the "MidCoastLab-Bootstrap"
scheduled task (SYSTEM, at startup) and starts it. Bootstrap is a state
machine persisted in C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\State\bootstrap.json, so
it resumes after every reboot.

Stages:  Common -> Role:<stage>... -> Validate -> Complete

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Retry` |  |  | Re-run after a failure, starting from the stage that failed. |

### `platform/validate.ps1`

Runs this machine's role validation on demand (outside bootstrap).

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

The orchestrator runs this as SYSTEM through the "MidCoastLab-Validate"
scheduled task, so checks that talk to other DCs use the computer account
instead of a remoting session that can't pass credentials on.
Writes Logs\Validation\latest.json.

### `platform/roles/dc.ps1`

DC role. Called by bootstrap.ps1 once per stage; returns the next stage.

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

metadata.dc_mode decides the path:
  Start turns on Remote Desktop (lab subnet, NLA) and installs AD DS and DNS.
  forest   Start -> Promote -> ConfigureDomain -> Finalize   (first DC ever)
  replica  Start -> Promote -> PostPromote     -> Finalize   (every other DC)

Secrets used (delivered by the orchestrator):
  forest:  domain_administrator, dsrm, every admin and service account
  replica: dsrm, svc-labdeploy
  both:    the Tailscale auth key, when site.yaml tailscale.enabled

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Metadata <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Inventory <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Stage <string>` | yes |  |  |

### `platform/roles/mgmt-tools.ps1`

Installs the MGMT toolchain. The single implementation, used by both the MGMT role (bootstrap, as SYSTEM) and setup/mgmt/Install-MgmtTools.ps1 (the one-time hand-build).

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

Inventory services: Git, Terraform, Packer, VSCode, RSAT. Plus what the
pipeline needs: PowerShell 7, KeePassXC, the Windows ADK Deployment Tools
(oscdimg.exe for Packer's generated CD), and the PowerShell modules
powershell-yaml, SecretManagement, SecretManagement.KeePass.

Direct vendor downloads, not winget: winget isn't reliably available to
SYSTEM. HashiCorp zips are checked against the published SHA256SUMS.
Every step is skipped when the tool is already present. Safe to re-run.

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Versions <object>` |  | `@{ git = 'latest'; terraform = 'latest'; packer = 'latest'; vscode = 'latest'; keepassxc = 'latest' }` | Hashtable or object with git, terraform, packer, vscode, keepassxc, each "latest" or an exact version (inventory: MGMT software_versions). Git for Windows and KeePassXC pins are release TAGS, e.g. "v2.47.1.windows.1" and "2.7.9"; HashiCorp and VS Code pins are plain versions. |
| `-Rsat <string[]>` |  | `@('standard')` | 'standard' (default): what the lab uses: AD DS/LDS, DNS, Group Policy, Server Manager. 'all': every RSAT tool Windows offers (3+ hours from Windows Update). Or capability names, e.g. 'Rsat.Dhcp.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0', alone or with 'standard'. |

### `platform/roles/mgmt.ps1`

MGMT role. Called by bootstrap.ps1 once per stage; returns the next stage.

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

Start -> Join -> Finalize

  Start     toolchain (mgmt-tools.ps1), Remote Desktop for admins
  Join      join the domain into the MGMT placement OU, with svc-domainjoin
  Finalize  Remote Desktop for the Tier 0 group, Group Policy (including
            LAPS), the tailnet, then validation

The handover of the repo, Terraform state and vault is NOT done here; the
outgoing MGMT pushes those during rotation (Invoke-LabMgmtRotation.ps1).
The hand-built MGMT-00 gets the equivalent of these stages from
setup/mgmt/Install-MgmtTools.ps1 and setup/mgmt/Join-LabDomain.ps1.

Secrets used: svc-domainjoin; the Tailscale auth key, when site.yaml tailscale.enabled

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Metadata <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Inventory <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Stage <string>` | yes |  |  |

### `platform/tailscale/Enable-LabTailscaleWatchdog.ps1`

Keeps this machine on the tailnet: a SYSTEM task that logs Tailscale back in whenever it has dropped out (after a restart, an update, a Tailscale upgrade).

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

On Windows, a login made with "tailscale up --authkey --unattended" doesn't
reliably survive a restart (tailscale/tailscale#3186), and the AuthKey system
policy didn't fix it on the first real lab either. So this installs a watchdog:

  C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Tailscale\
    authkey.bin    the auth key, DPAPI-encrypted for this machine
    watchdog.json  hostname
    watchdog.ps1   checks "tailscale status"; NeedsLogin/Stopped -> "tailscale up"
    watchdog.log   what it did (kept under 1 MB)

The folder is readable by SYSTEM and Administrators only. The scheduled task
"MidCoastLab-Tailscale" runs watchdog.ps1 as SYSTEM 2 minutes after every start
and every 15 minutes. The same flags as the first join: --unattended
--accept-routes=false --accept-dns=false --hostname=<name>.

Run it on a lab machine that's already on the tailnet (from MGMT, for an
existing machine):
  Invoke-Command -ComputerName <ip> -UseSSL -SessionOption $o -Credential <you>-a `
      -FilePath ./platform/tailscale/Enable-LabTailscaleWatchdog.ps1 -ArgumentList $key
New machines get it from the pipeline (Lab.System Install-LabTailscale).

-Remove takes it all away (retiring a machine).

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-AuthKey <string>` |  |  |  |
| `-Hostname <string>` |  | `$env:COMPUTERNAME` |  |
| `-Remove` |  |  |  |

### `platform/validation/dc-validation.ps1`

DC validation. Returns a report object and writes JSON to C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Logs\Validation (latest.json + timestamped).

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

Runs as SYSTEM (read-only checks). The common checks (NET, TS, MEM, EVAL)
come from Lab.Validation; this file adds the directory, DNS, SYSVOL, FSMO,
replication, time, LAPS and Remote Desktop checks. Severity and recovery
actions come from catalog.psd1. To run it by hand on a DC:
    C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Platform\validate.ps1

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Metadata <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Inventory <object>` | yes |  |  |

### `platform/validation/mgmt-validation.ps1`

MGMT validation: toolchain, domain membership, and reach to everything MGMT manages (DCs over WinRM/HTTPS, the Proxmox API). Runs as SYSTEM.

Runs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7.

The common checks (NET, TS, MEM, EVAL) come from Lab.Validation; this file
adds MGMT-001..007. Severity and recovery actions come from catalog.psd1.
Writes Logs\Validation\latest.json. To run it by hand on MGMT:
    C:\ProgramData\MidCoastLab\Platform\validate.ps1

| Parameter | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-Metadata <object>` | yes |  |  |
| `-Inventory <object>` | yes |  |  |

## Packer: inside the template build

Run by Packer inside the build VM (`Build-LabTemplate.ps1` starts Packer). Not run by hand.

### `packer/windows/files/build-bootstrap.ps1`

First-logon script of the Packer BUILD VM (from the generated answer CD).

Runs once, inside the build VM, before Packer connects: installs the VirtIO
guest tools (with the QEMU guest agent Packer uses to find the VM's address
and the balloon service), keeps a Windows client image sysprep-safe and
unencrypted, and opens a build-only WinRM/HTTPS listener for Packer.
Initialize-LabRemoting.ps1 replaces that listener on each clone's first boot.

### `packer/windows/scripts/Finalize-Template.ps1`

Packer provisioner, last step: clean up, enable Cloudbase-Init, sysprep /generalize.

Checks the staged files are there, records template provenance, removes
per-user packages that make sysprep fail, refuses a BitLocker-encrypted
image, cleans temp files and the component store, forgets the build VM's
DHCP lease (so clones ask for a fresh one), then runs sysprep /generalize
/oobe /quit, up to three times, removing a package sysprep names as the
blocker between tries. /quit keeps this WinRM session alive; Packer then
stops the VM and converts it to a template.

### `packer/windows/scripts/Install-LabSoftware.ps1`

Packer provisioner: installs PowerShell 7 and Cloudbase-Init into the template.

Versions come from inventory (templates.<key>.build.software_versions) through
the environment variables LAB_PWSH_VERSION and LAB_CBI_CHANNEL, which
windows.pkr.hcl sets. Cloudbase-Init is installed but left stopped: it runs
on clones, not during the build.
